claims.statement: Allen et al. (arXiv 1906.01036v1 = PLoS Comput. Biol. 16(1):e1007529): model (connected undirected unweighted graph without loops, death-Birth updating, one mutant at a uniformly random vertex, fitness r = 1 + delta), coalescence-time equations (5), remeeting times (6), N_eff = sum pi_i tau_i (9), and the definition: G is an amplifier of weak selection iff N_eff > N, a suppressor iff N_eff < N.
Allen et al. eq. (8): rho_G(1+delta) = 1/N + delta (N_eff - 2)/(2N) + O(delta^2); hence N_eff > N implies rho_G(r) > rho_{K_N}(r) for r in (1, b) for some b > 1 and rho_G < rho_K on (a, 1).

Richter, arXiv:2204.12861v1, p. 8, Fig. 1: four non-isomorphic N = 11 transient amplifiers (a)-(d) printed with N_eff 11.0008, 11.0128, 11.0056, 11.0952 and mean degrees 3.8182, 2.9091, 3.0909, 2.9091; the caption and the text (p. 8) state that all four have maximum degree 4, and the text (p. 8, p. 10, caption of Fig. 2(b)) states that (b), at 11.0128, has the highest N_eff; p. 10 prints the mean degree of (b) and (d) as 2.0991 against 2.9091 in the caption. Minimum degrees 3, 2, 2, 2 and normalized-Laplacian lambda_2 0.0567, 0.0399, 0.0451, 0.0481 are printed for (a)-(d).

Enumeration: nauty geng 2.7r3, geng -c 11 res/256 for res = 0..255, each part piped into the checker; the per-part '>Z k graphs generated' lines (logs/parts/) equal the number of graphs decided; the 256 parts sum to 1,006,700,565 = OEIS A001349(11) (read on oeis.org in the session). Completeness rests on geng and on this count; not kernel-checked.

Census: among the 1,006,700,565 connected graphs on 11 vertices, exactly 4 have N_eff > 11, exactly 539 have N_eff = 11 (all regular), and 1,006,700,022 have N_eff < 11, each certified by an exact integer inequality (float64 Cholesky proposal rounded to 2^-30, exact __int128 residual, non-negativity of the inverse of I - M turns the residual into an error bound; guard |x| 2^30 < 2^50). 543 non-excluded graphs (539 regular + 4) were solved exactly with Fractions. guard_fail 0, chol_fail 0, largest eps 7.45e-8. Smallest certified gap over excluded graphs 0.0020643. NOT kernel-checked; the decision rule is C1's hand-proved bound (audited there), the C implementation is validated against the Python code but not independently audited.

Validation of the C port before any N = 11 use: against C1's data at N = 3..10 (inputs sha256-equal to C1's geng files) identical graph counts, excluded counts and candidate sets; per-graph comparison with the guarded Python functions on all graphs at N = 3..9 and a 10^6-graph stride sample at N = 10, 0 verdict mismatches, certified intervals intersect on every graph, max |dN_eff_hat| 1.1e-10; exact finish reproduces C1 (0 amplifiers, ties 1,2,2,5,4,17,22,167 = A005177); on a 10^7-graph N = 11 sample the Python and C codes give identical counts (9,999,998 excluded) and candidate sets. A bug was found and fixed before validation: the first build did not JSON-escape the backslash character that graph6 can contain (characters 63..126); output formatting only, the 10^7 throughput run used that first build and its decisions are unaffected; validation, controls and the census used the fixed build (sha256 6f658a78...).

The 539 ties are exactly the connected regular graphs on 11 vertices: 539 = OEIS A005177(11) (read on oeis.org in the session), and no non-regular graph has N_eff = 11 (exact_candidates_eq_nonregular = 0).

Exact N_eff of the four amplifiers (Fraction solves with C1's dbcore.neff_exact, and a second pure-Fraction Gauss-Jordan exact_census.py on eqs. (5), (6), (9) that gives the same four graphs and the same maximum): R11 (JCQRRQodIU? = J?ouPjI[@i?, 21 edges) 2668552698098/242579025123 = 11.000756; A2 (J?`CP_p[C[?, 16 edges) 2890154941667179019/262436329991601232 = 11.012785; A3 (J?`@`eoRAW_, 17 edges) 88175846355074579/8011935789939084 = 11.005561; A1 (J?`@`eoRAW?, 16 edges) 328435957/29601736 = 11.095159. The four have distinct nauty labelg canonical forms and are pairwise non-isomorphic by networkx; only JCQRRQodIU? is isomorphic to J?ouPjI[@i?. For R11 the Tier A statement is C1's R11_amplifier (doi 10.5281/zenodo.23704563), not re-checked in this ledger; for A1-A3 see AMN-A-0001..0003.

Nearest non-amplifiers (exact Fractions, the 10 non-regular graphs with the smallest certified gap): the closest is J?`bJaWeJK? with N_eff = 345273648427163/31394406114960 = 10.997935 (20 edges); no graph had a certified upper bound within 1e-3 of 11 (near_graphs 0).

Match with Richter 2022 Fig. 1: the four amplifiers correspond to (a)-(d) by printed N_eff (11.0008, 11.0128, 11.0056, 11.0952; ours 11.000756, 11.012785, 11.005561, 11.095159), mean degree (2m/11 = 3.8182, 2.9091, 3.0909, 2.9091 from edge counts 21, 16, 17, 16), minimum degree (3, 2, 2, 2) and normalized-Laplacian lambda_2 (0.0567, 0.0399, 0.0451, 0.0481 for R11, A2, A3, A1; AUDIT.md C3). Drawings were NOT compared. So the four graphs are not new; the exhaustiveness at N = 11 is what the census adds, to our knowledge.

Finite-r signs of rho_G - rho_{K11} on the exact 2046-state dB chain (float LU proposal, exact-rational residual bound, error <= 3.9e-14): A1 +4.2836e-6 at r = 1001/1000, -4.3668e-6 at 999/1000, +4.3212e-7 at 10001/10000; A2 +5.2504e-7, -6.3683e-7, +5.7556e-8; A3 +2.0120e-7, -3.0395e-7, +2.4762e-8. At r = 1.0001, A1: first-order prediction 4.325e-7, measured 4.321e-7. Certified at these three r only; no r_max is computed for A1-A3. Python Fractions, not kernel-checked.

Controls run before the N = 11 census (positive): K11 and C11 not excluded, exact N_eff = 11; Richter's graph not excluded, exact value as above, its quartic parent exactly 11; enumeration level: all 4,721 connected graphs with degrees in [3,4] and 21 edges (geng -c -d3 -D4 11 21:21) give exactly one candidate, JCQRRQodIU?, canonical form equal to that of J?ouPjI[@i?; C1's 14 controls re-run from a copy, all met. (Negative): corrupted criterion pi_i = 1/N through the same certified path gives 9 new candidates at N = 10 (e.g. I?`CP`ce_ with corrupted value 10.0193 > 10 against the correct 9.6643); the strict test N_eff > N rejects K11, C11 and the parent.

Three internal inconsistencies in Richter 2022 Fig. 1 (observations): (1) the caption and the text of p. 8 say all four graphs have maximum degree 4, but our A1 (his (d), 11.0952) has maximum degree 3: it is A3 with the edge between A3's two degree-4 vertices removed (the graph6 strings differ in one bit), which fits his own remark that (d) is (c) minus the red edge; (2) the text (p. 8, p. 10, caption of Fig. 2(b)) says (b), at 11.0128, has the highest N_eff, but (d) has 11.0952; (3) p. 10 prints the mean degree of (b) and (d) as 2.0991, against 2.9091 in the caption of Fig. 1. Neither affects the census; neither has been raised with the author.

HEADLINE. Among the 1,006,700,565 connected unweighted simple graphs on 11 vertices there are exactly four with Allen's N_eff > N, that is, exactly four unweighted death-Birth amplifiers of weak selection at N = 11 (exact rational N_eff); 539 tie (all regular, = A005177(11)); the rest are below. They are the four N = 11 graphs of Richter 2022 Fig. 1, matched by N_eff, edges and degrees (not by drawings). Filed C because the census half is.
